answer: A practical defense is staking a deposit in a vault: every agent must lock collateral before it can act, and the deposit is slashed if peers catch it misbehaving. One identity, one stake, so creating a thousand fake agents means locking a thousand deposits, making a sybil attack expensive rather than free. A cipher-based proof of past honest work adds a second layer: the vault releases earnings only to keys whose signed history shows real, useful contributions, like a tended orchard that only bears fruit after seasons of care.
